open_questions: Impact parameter b=0.9617 is grazing; precise ephemeris and radius require follow-up to confirm flat ingress despite short duration.
Centroid inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) – ground-based photometry needed to confirm on-target and rule out resolved blend at >21 arcsec.
Rotation vs period not tested – spot checks can test if 11.9 d is harmonic of stellar variability, though phase_curve ratio_to_depth 0.05809 is low.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 2269 ppm, flat-bottomed 11.9-day dip repeating four times on this K dwarf with a 3.3 Earth-radius size, no odd-even difference and no secondary eclipse. No nearby star within a pixel can mimic it and the depth is steady. The very short, grazing transit remains puzzling but looks best as a small planet until follow-up confirms it on target.

reasons.why: Super-Earth radius well below stellar range favours planet over EB; xgboost low score partly driven by other metrics but size positively favours planet.
Flat bottom (negative v_sigma) favours transiting planet; despite high impact parameter b=0.9617, grazing planet can still be flat-bottomed.
No significant odd/even difference, not a binary at twice period.
No significant secondary (below 5 sigma and below best_brightening_snr), ruling out deep stellar secondary eclipse.
No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the dip with a plausible eclipse depth, and centroid is inconclusive with no clear off-target.
Depth steady between sectors (2345 ppm vs 1878 ppm, chi2 1.258) so not a few bad events or variable blend.
Short duration noted but fit_log_density_ratio -0.7662 and star_density_penalty 2.32; grazing/high impact transit common for flat-bottoms and does not alone indicate binary.
